title: Minor Maintenance: Changing Lightbulbs
blurb: How to change a lightbulb safely: power off, bulb cool, the right steps, the right bulb and safe disposal.
siteNotes: Who is allowed to change bulbs, and which fittings (high ceilings, specialist fittings) are for maintenance only
Where step-ladders are kept, and where spare bulbs of the correct type are stored
Who in maintenance to report a damaged, scorched or loose fitting to
How old bulbs and fluorescent tubes are disposed of here
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-30. Electricity: Electricity at Work Regulations 1989. Working at height: Work at Height Regulations 2005. Disposal of old lamps: waste regulations (some lamp types are hazardous or electrical waste).

CHECK: the trainer says some bulbs, such as fluorescent tubes, need special disposal. Confirm which types the venue uses and the correct waste route (for example separate collection for fluorescent tubes).

CHECK: the trainer says to isolate the light "where you can". Confirm who is competent to isolate a circuit at the venue, and that staff are not expected to touch wiring or open fittings beyond swapping a bulb.

cards.title: Minor Maintenance: Changing Lightbulbs
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- make the power safe and let the bulb cool
- use the right access and the right replacement
- report a damaged fitting instead of forcing it

cards.title: The simplest job in the world
cards.body: Changing a lightbulb sounds like the simplest job in the world, which is exactly why people get hurt doing it. It combines two hazards we have already covered, electricity and working at height, and adds a hot bulb. Slow down, and a two-minute job stays a two-minute job.

cards.title: Off, isolated, cooled
cards.body: Switch the light off and, where you can, isolate it properly so it cannot be turned back on while you are working. Give a hot bulb time to cool. A bulb that has been on can easily burn your fingers, and a startled jump up a ladder is how falls happen.

items.title: Switch off
items.text: And isolate it where you can

items.title: Stop it being switched on
items.text: Nobody can turn it back on while you work

cards.title: Right steps, firm ground
cards.body: Use the correct step-ladder or steps for the height. Never a chair, a table or a wobbly stool. Set it up on firm, level ground. For a high or awkward fitting, get someone to steady the ladder and keep three points of contact.

left.title: Use
items: Someone steadying it for high fittings

cards.title: Right bulb, safe disposal
cards.body: Use the correct replacement: the right type, fitting and wattage. The wrong bulb can overheat or damage the fitting. Dispose of the old bulb safely, as some types, like fluorescent tubes, need special disposal.

cards.title: Do not force it
cards.body: If the fitting itself looks damaged, scorched or loose, do not force it. Stop and report it to maintenance.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Switch off, and isolate where you can. Let a hot bulb cool.
- Correct step-ladder or steps on firm, level ground. Never a chair, table or stool.
- For a high fitting, have someone steady the ladder and keep three points of contact.
- Correct type, fitting and wattage. Dispose of old bulbs safely.
- Damaged, scorched or loose fitting: stop and report it to maintenance.

cards.q: Before changing a bulb, what should you do with the power?
options: Leave it on so you can see the fitting
Dim it to the lowest setting
Turn it down and unscrew carefully
Switch it off and isolate it
cards.why: Switch the light off and, where you can, isolate it so it cannot be turned back on while you work.

cards.q: You should let a hot bulb cool before touching it.
cards.why: A hot bulb can easily burn your fingers, and a startled jump up a ladder is how falls happen.

cards.q: To reach a ceiling light you should use…
options: A chair from the dining room
cards.why: Use the correct step-ladder or steps for the height, never a chair, a table or a wobbly stool.

cards.q: Any bulb will do as long as it fits the socket.
cards.why: Use the right type, fitting and wattage. The wrong bulb can overheat or damage the fitting.

cards.q: Which other two hazards does a lightbulb change combine, besides the hot bulb?
cards.why: It combines electricity and working at height, and adds a hot bulb.

cards.q: A damaged or scorched light fitting should be…
cards.why: Do not force it. Stop and report it to maintenance.

cards.q: Some old bulbs (such as fluorescent tubes) need special disposal.
cards.why: Dispose of the old bulb safely, as some types need special disposal.

options: Any spare that is to hand
The correct type, fitting and wattage
cards.why: Use the correct type, fitting and wattage, because the wrong bulb can overheat or damage the fitting.

cards.q: Rushing a simple job like this can lead to burns or falls.
cards.why: Slow down: a hot bulb and a ladder are exactly how burns and falls happen.

cards.q: Why get someone to steady the ladder for a high fitting?
options: To pass up the bulb faster
To check the wiring behind it
To keep it stable and prevent a fall
To hold the old bulb as you swap
cards.why: For a high or awkward fitting, someone steadying the ladder helps keep it stable and prevents a fall.
